solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Conservative's opening game is pathetic

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only the start of the word is wanted

parts.note: the initial letter of the party name
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Tories' opening move in politics is feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening game' reads as a gambit in a match, but 'opening' belongs with 'Conservative's' and the game is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal slang for poor, shoddy or contemptibly bad, a close synonym.

clue.text: Sex: Republicans have the edge here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sexual intercourse, in a formal old-fashioned word
second meaning: the US legislature, where the Republican party held the majority

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that Republicans are the better lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boast about bedroom prowess; the second half is really a description of the American legislature with a Republican majority.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is a formal term for sexual union and also the bicameral American legislative body.

clue.text: Government's planned action: cut-back biting

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is written from its end

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
a biting wind is icy cold

explanation.surface: A government announces spending cuts that will hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-back' looks like one word for austerity, but it splits into a word for cut and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy is a course of action adopted and planned by a government or party.

clue.text: Arsy-versy clanger Corbyn initially dropped concerning what the Queen does

indicators.note: arsy-versy is slang for back to front or upside down
something dropped is let fall and left out, so a letter goes

parts.note: taken as written; a clanger is a blunder

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the initial letter of the Labour leader's name

explanation.surface: Corbyn makes a back-to-front gaffe about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' picks the first letter of Corbyn, and that letter is removed from the blunder before the rest is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnal is the adjective relating to a reign, the thing a monarch does, as in regnal years.

clue.text: Bad poetry and heartless drivel about poor George

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
with no heart the middle is gone, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: something in poor shape is damaged, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic says some bad verse about poor George is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged name sits inside the outer letters of drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is comic or clumsily written verse, crude poetry with irregular rhythm.

clue.text: Fusses about end of Labour's Ed and David?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to bother is to fuss

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Commotion surrounding the two Labour men Ed and David Miliband.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed and David Miliband, rival candidates for Labour leader in 2010, are siblings; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed and David Miliband are a famous pair of male siblings, an example of the plural noun.

clue.text: Corbyn's just started a right load of malarkey as an "inducement"

indicators.note: something just started has only its beginning in place

parts.note: the first letter of the name
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Corbyn offers a lot of nonsense to tempt voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right load of malarkey' looks like one phrase meaning utter nonsense, but 'right' is a separate abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot, as in carrot and stick, is an incentive offered to persuade someone.

clue.text: Tuck member under bed with no base

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom, so the last letter goes
in a down entry, going under means being placed after

parts.note: a crib is a baby's bed
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a body part beneath a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a limb, but it is the parliamentary member, placed below the shortened bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to press into small folds or pleats, a kind of tucking of material.

clue.text: (& 16ac.) Go the apparent way of Trump and Kim Jong-Un, mentally, and mislay one's sculptures?

definitions.text: Go the apparent way of Trump and Kim Jong-Un, mentally
definitions.meaning: first meaning: go mad, the idiom for losing one's sanity
second meaning, literal: sculptures carved in marble, such as the Elgin collection, go missing

explanation.surface: A dig at the sanity of two nuclear-armed leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical literal reading, with marble carvings standing in for the toy balls of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become insane, while literally it describes misplacing statues carved from stone.

clue.text: President Trump's fourth out-of-control "narco"

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild and land in a new order
fourth picks a single letter by its position in the word

parts.note: the fourth letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A headline calling a president a drug runner gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Trump' reads as one name, but 'President' is the definition and Trump only lends a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is the French head of state, so the surname fits a presidential definition.

clue.text: Many Brexiteers unhappy with this timing, or am I mistaken?

indicators.note: something mistaken has gone wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Leave voters are unhappy about the timing of Brexit, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This timing' looks like it refers to Brexit's schedule; the definition stops at 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern about people arriving to settle in Britain was a major motive for many Leave voters.

clue.text: (& 23ac.) Grand, not small, testes (nuts) — prepare yourself

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild
not means without, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A crude boast about large testicles, with a warning to brace oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' in brackets looks like slang for the testes, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Get set is the middle call in 'ready, steady, go', telling people to get ready.

clue.text: Already pissed in the outskirts of Purley, really suffer for your actions

indicators.note: in means placed inside something else
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters; Purley is a suburb of south London

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk in the London suburbs faces the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Already' looks like an adverb about timing, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay dearly is an idiom for facing harsh consequences or a heavy cost because of one's deeds.

clue.text: Generous booze shifts butt to the middle

indicators.note: moving something to the middle sets it inside the rest
shifting a thing takes it out of its old position

parts.note: lager is beer
the butt is the end, here the final letter of the drink

explanation.surface: A drinker's beer belly moves to the middle, after a generous measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a backside, but it means the end of the drink's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean liberal or generous in spirit, as in large-hearted.

clue.text: US president who's a pain in the arse for May?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Andrew or Lyndon B, both presidents of the United States

definitions.text: who's a pain in the arse for May?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Boris, the Foreign Secretary who troubled Theresa May

explanation.surface: A US president making life hard for Theresa May.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies Trump, but the answer is a surname shared by two former US presidents and May's troublesome rival Boris.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to past American leaders and to the British minister who undermined the Prime Minister.

clue.text: Small balls bump means sod all

parts.note: the jack is the small target ball in bowls
to bump is to hit

explanation.surface: A crude remark that a little knock to the testicles is nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small balls' suggests testicles, but the balls are the targets in bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are vulgar slang for nothing at all; sod all is the British version.

clue.text: Success with sex turned sour? Get on

parts.note: a hit is a success
it is slang for sex
milk that has turned sour has gone off

explanation.surface: A successful sex life turned bad; time to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' looks like advice to move on, but it means to be friendly with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit it off is to form a good rapport and quickly become friendly.

clue.text: see 8ac
Deranged piece by Independent (state backed)

parts.note: a chess piece is a man
I is the abbreviation for Independent

indicators.note: backed means sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: CA is the postal code for California

explanation.surface: A mad article in the Independent newspaper backed by the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a newspaper article, but it is a chess or draughts piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Maniac can be an adjective meaning wildly insane or frenzied, like maniacal.

clue.text: Dismissed what Charles hopes his mother will be before too long?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excluded as a possibility

definitions.text: what Charles hopes his mother will be before too long?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: the Queen having finished her reign so her heir can take over

explanation.surface: Prince Charles's impatience to succeed his mother the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a monarch who has done all her ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled out means rejected or excluded, while literally it describes a reign that has come to its end.

clue.text: Interrupt Conservative leader who's powerless

indicators.note: without power means the letter standing for power is removed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
Vladimir Putin, Russia's leader

explanation.surface: Heckling a weak Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative leader' looks like one phrase, but the leader is Russia's, who loses the P that stands for power.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is a phrasal verb for interrupting someone while they are speaking.

clue.text: Part reduction of earnings? Definitely not!

indicators.note: a part is only a portion, so the letters lie inside a longer stretch

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they'd take a pay cut replies with a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: No fear! is British informal for certainly not.
explanation.definitionFit: No fear is a colloquial British exclamation of emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Tedious spiel about mug with one loo

indicators.note: about can mean round and round, so the letters are turned every which way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boring talk about a cup and a single toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two lots of letters that are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by one person, often tiresome to listeners.

clue.text: Thatcher's Left side accepted latitude

indicators.note: the left side of a word is its first half, read from the start

parts.note: the first half of Margaret, Mrs Thatcher's first name
in means fashionable or accepted

explanation.surface: Thatcher's leftist wing tolerated some leeway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left side' sounds political, and a margin is a left side of a page, but here it takes the first half of Margaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Margin and latitude both mean freedom or leeway to act, as in a margin for error.

clue.text: Inept Hague out to suppress leader of Conservatives

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, keeping one piece held within the other
out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; William Hague, former Tory leader

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Clumsy William Hague, ousted, crushes the Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague was a Conservative party leader, so the surface reads as party infighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward or clumsy, lacking grace or tact.

clue.text: Torture in alien nation

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ET is the film alien
gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: Torture practised in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien nation' reads as a foreign land, but the alien is the film character and only 'nation' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a North African country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: see 11ac,
Kindle article on Democrat "vengeful figure" that doesn't put Trump in a good light

definitions.text: that doesn't put Trump in a good light

parts.note: to kindle is to set on fire
an indefinite article
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
the Furies were avenging spirits of Greek myth

explanation.surface: An e-book about a Democrat's revenge that embarrasses Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' suggests Amazon's e-reader, fitting the book theme, but it is the verb. The definition is a description of Michael Wolff's 2018 exposé of Trump's White House.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire and Fury is Michael Wolff's unflattering book about Trump's first year as president.

clue.text: If in drag, jogging is improper

indicators.note: jogging jolts things, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Going for a run while cross-dressed is unseemly.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra dig, short for Latin infra dignitatem, is a British phrase for something beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath one's dignity is unbecoming and so unsuitable or unseemly behaviour.

clue.text: Tabloid: "Hot, advanced temperature beachwear?"

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
A is the abbreviation for advanced
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline promising a heatwave and swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: headgear worn at the beach is one kind of beachwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed hat protecting against the sun is typically worn at the seaside.
